27-120.r: Judicial Activism in India → linked to Public Interest Litigation; began in the mid 1970s on the Supreme Court's initiative.

27-121.r: 'Judicial activism should not become judicial adventurism' → Justice A.S. Anand; adventurism is an extreme form of activism.

27-122.r: 23 September 2003 → Supreme Court (Justice M.B. Shah) glorified women's status: preferring women as Principal of Government Girls' College does not violate Articles 14, 15, 16.

27-123.r: Vishakha vs State of Rajasthan → guidelines against sexual harassment of women at workplace (1997); superseded by Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013.

27-124.r: Triple Talaq (Talaq-e-Biddat) → declared unconstitutional in Shayara Bano case (2017) as violating Article 14; Parliament's Triple Talaq Law endorsed it.

27-125.r: CBI called a 'Caged Parrot' by Supreme Court → Coal Gate (coal allocation) scam case.

27-126.r: Supreme Court judgement on homosexuality → Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
27-126.t: It is Section 377 of IPC, not an Article 377 or 277 of the Constitution.

27-127.r: All proceedings in Supreme Court and every High Court in English → Article 348(1)(a).

28-001.r: Elected Governor plan dropped → it meant another election; elected Governor might feel superior to CM; Governor works under Parliamentary System. Governor is appointed by President.

28-006.r: Governor (Article 157) → Indian citizen (birth not required), at least 35 years; not member of either House (Article 158); can be Governor of two or more States.

28-008.r: Governor's oath (Article 159) → before Chief Justice of the High Court, or in his absence senior-most Judge; oath form is in Article 159, not Third Schedule.
28-008.t: Governor's oath form is in Article 159 itself, not in the Third Schedule.

28-010.r: Article 153 → Governor for each State; 154 → executive power; 155 → appointment (not removal); 156 → term of office.
28-010.h: 153 office, 154 power, 155 appointment, 156 term: the Governor's story in order.

28-012.r: Article 153 → a Governor for each State; Seventh Amendment (1956) allowed one person as Governor of two or more States → A false, R true.

28-013.r: Governor → appointed by President, can govern more than one State, five-year term at President's pleasure (Article 156(1)); State Legislature cannot remove him.

28-014.r: Article 156 → Governor holds office at President's pleasure (removable any time) and may continue beyond five years till successor takes over; neither statement follows.

28-015.r: Governor → responsible to the President; holds office at President's pleasure (Article 156(1)), in effect the Union Government; term five years (Article 156(3)).

28-017.r: Constitution lays down no procedure for removing a Governor; same person can govern two or more States; HC Judges appointed by President, Governor consulted.

28-018.r: Governor of Jammu & Kashmir → appointed by President; J&K had special status under Article 370 (Part XXI); before 1965 its head was elected by the Assembly.

28-019.r: J&K head renamed from Sadar-e-Riyasat to Governor in 1965 → 6th Amendment of J&K State Constitution; after J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 → Lieutenant Governors.

28-020.r: Rajpramukh (1949-1956) abolished on States Reorganisation Commission advice (Fazal Ali, K.M. Panikkar, H.N. Kunzru; set up December 1953) via 7th Amendment; Governor instead.

28-021.r: Union Territories → administered by the President through an administrator appointed by him (Article 239(1)).

28-022.r: First Lieutenant Governor of UT of Jammu & Kashmir → Girish Chandra Murmu; Manoj Sinha became the 2nd on 7 August 2020.

28-023.r: First Lieutenant Governor of UT of Ladakh → Radha Krishna Mathur (from 31 October 2019); Kavinder Gupta took office July 2025.
28-023.t: G.C. Murmu was the first LG of Jammu & Kashmir, not Ladakh.

28-024.r: Governor's emoluments and allowances → charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State (Article 202(3)(a)).
hi: Consolidated Fund of the State (राज्य की संचित निधि)

28-025.r: Same Governor for two or more States → emoluments shared among States in proportion fixed by President's order (Article 158(3A)).

28-026.r: Governor's discretionary powers → report to President for President's Rule (Article 356) and reserving State bills for President; not appointing Ministers or making business rules.

28-027.r: Governor's discretion → asking Government to prove majority, dismissing CM who lost confidence, reserving a Bill for President, returning a Bill (Article 200); not consulting High Court.

28-028.r: Article 163(1) → Constitution explicitly lets Governor act in his discretion in some spheres; President cannot on his own reserve a State bill not forwarded by Governor.

28-029.r: Article 200 → Governor can return an ordinary bill (not money bill) for reconsideration or reserve it for President; no time limit fixed for returning it.
28-029.t: Don't pick one or three months: the Constitution fixes no time limit.

28-033.r: Rajasthan bill passed without the Governor's required recommendation → once the Governor gives assent, the Act is not invalid.

28-034.r: Article 213 → Governor promulgates ordinances during recess of Legislature; must be laid before State Legislature and approved by it, else it ceases to operate.

28-037.r: Governor's ordinance power → Article 213; 155 → appointment of Governor; 156 → term; 212 → courts cannot inquire into Legislature's proceedings.

28-038.r: High Court Judges → appointed by President (consulting CJI, Governor, HC Chief Justice), not Governor; Governor appoints CM, State PSC members, Advocate General.

28-039.r: Governor does not appoint HC Judges (Article 217(1)) and nominates some Legislative Council members; he is part of the Legislature and has judicial powers.

28-040.r: Governor (Article 161) can pardon, remit, commute sentences but cannot pardon a death sentence; he is part of State Legislature, no Emergency powers.
28-040.t: Death sentence pardon is with the President, not the Governor.

28-041.r: Article 361(2) → no criminal case against President/Governor during term; civil case allowed after two months' written notice (361(4)) → A false; President impeachable (Article 61).

28-042.r: Governor → no criminal proceedings during term (Article 361); emoluments cannot be diminished during term (Article 158(4)); both statements correct.

28-043.r: Article 361(1) → Governor not answerable to any court for official acts; 361(2) → no criminal proceedings during term; State legislators immune for anything said in House.

28-044.r: Courts cannot inquire into advice given by Ministers to the President (Article 74(2)); President/Governor immune for official acts; two months' notice for civil suits.

28-045.r: No impeachment provision for a Governor (holds office at President's pleasure); President → impeachment (Article 61); Vice-President → resolution of Council of States.

28-046.r: First woman Governor of a State → Sarojini Naidu, Governor of Uttar Pradesh (United Province) after Independence; died in office in 1949.

28-048.r: National Women's Day, 13 February → birth date of Sarojini Naidu (born 13 February 1879; died 2 March 1949), India's first woman Governor.

28-049.r: First woman Governor of West Bengal → Padmaja Naidu (1956-1967), daughter of Sarojini Naidu; first Governor of West Bengal → Chakravarti Rajagopalachari.

28-050.r: First woman Governor of Madhya Pradesh → Sarla Grewal (1989-1990), 9th Governor; second woman IAS officer (1952). Droupadi Murmu was Jharkhand Governor (2015-2021).

28-051.r: MP Governors H.V. Pataskar, K.C. Reddy, Satyanarayan Sinha were Constituent Assembly members; Niranjan Nath Wanchoo was not.
28-051.c: No answer printed (*): only Wanchoo was not a member, so none of the options is correct.

28-052.r: Dr. Bhagwat Dayal Sharma → first CM of Haryana (1966-67); Governor of Odisha (1977-80) and Madhya Pradesh (1980-84).

28-053.r: First Governor of Rajasthan → Gurumukh Nihal Singh, appointed 25 October 1956 (not 1 November); Rajpramukh abolished by 7th Amendment from 1 November 1956.

28-054.r: Raghukul Tilak → Rajasthan Governor dismissed in August 1981; first Governor ever dismissed → Prabhudas Patwari of Tamil Nadu (October 1980).

28-055.r: Correct pairs: Rajasthan → Kalraj Mishra; Uttar Pradesh → Anandiben Patel. West Bengal → C.V. Ananda Bose and Gujarat → Acharya Devvrat (not Satya Pal Malik, Phagu Chauhan).

28-056.r: Sarkaria Commission (1983; report 1988) → Governor: eminent person from outside the State, detached, without intense or recent political links; CM to have a say.

29-001.r: State Legislature (Article 168) → Governor + Legislative Assembly (+ Legislative Council where it exists); bicameral: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh.

29-002.r: Upper House of a State Legislature → Legislative Council; lower → Legislative Assembly; with only one House it is the Legislative Assembly (Article 168(2)).

29-003.r: Article 171 → composition of Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad); Article 169 → its creation and abolition.
29-003.t: Don't mix 169 (create/abolish the Council) with 171 (its composition).

29-004.r: Create/abolish State Legislative Council (Article 169) → Assembly resolution by majority of total membership and two-thirds present and voting, then a law by Parliament.

29-010.r: Article 169 resolution to abolish a State Legislative Council → Union Government is not obliged to start legislation in Parliament.

29-011.r: Legislative Council size (Article 171) → not more than one-third of Assembly's total membership, and never less than forty.
29-011.h: Ceiling one-third of Assembly, floor forty.

29-012.r: Legislative Council → max one-third of Assembly strength, so never larger than half; Governor does not nominate its Chairman; Assembly: 60 to 500 members (Article 170(1)).
